learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected about fifty percent and locked it in.
observations.exploration: Ran ten-thousand web replies: 32.3 percent support. One-thousand web: 35.3. One-hundred-thousand web: 33.1. One-thousand random calls: 48.7. Bars accumulated with narrower web whiskers at larger sizes. No reset or repeated new sample control visible; completed all four presets.
observations.reveal: Corrected to about thirty-three percent, explained twice-likely opposition response and more replies narrowing uncertainty around biased estimate. Compared random calls near truth through equal selection chances.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshots inspected. Four horizontal bars, percentage labels, whiskers and dashed town-fifty-percent line visible. Reveal readable. Whisker meaning and confidence level not explicitly defined in learner text.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviews inspected.

prediction.reason: Concrete response-rate imbalance supports a selection-bias commitment.
prediction.evidence: Equal town split but opponents twice as likely to respond.

interaction.reason: Three web sizes and random-call comparison separate sample size from selection.
interaction.evidence: 33.1 at one hundred thousand web versus 48.7 at one thousand calls.

payoff.reason: Reveal explains precision around a biased target.
payoff.evidence: Whiskers shrink while web estimates stay near one third.

clarity.reason: Comparison is strong but whiskers are undefined and every-batch ratio prose overstates expected behavior.
clarity.evidence: Observed web values vary around one third, while prose says every batch has two opponents per backer.

transfer.reason: General sample-selection principle stated within same poll without a new application.
transfer.evidence: Equal chance of being asked versus self-selection.

accessibility.evidence: Selected poll percentage exposed as text; keyboard, screen reader, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: A hundred times more web replies remain systematically off target.

visualExplanation.reason: Tightening whiskers away from truth separates uncertainty and bias.
visualExplanation.evidence: Dashed fifty-percent line against web bars.

playfulness.reason: Four sampling presets accumulate a comparison.
playfulness.evidence: Three sizes and one alternative method.

practicalValue.reason: Useful for judging large voluntary-response polls.
practicalValue.evidence: Selection process matters more than reply count here.

depth.reason: Distinguishes sampling precision and systematic selection error.

complexity.reason: Simple presets introduce bias versus sampling uncertainty.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Normalize unequal response propensities and distinguish precision from representativeness.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Four fixed poll buttons, no visible reset.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Percentages, sample-size powers of ten and horizontal intervals.

whyCool: A narrower uncertainty bar can sit confidently around the wrong target.
caveat: Whisker confidence level is not stated and ratio language should describe expectation rather than every realized batch.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
